sections.title: I. Macroeconomic Developments
sections.description: GDP growth, inflation, exchange rate, monetary policy, fiscal position, key sector performance

events.title: IMF Concludes Article IV Consultation: Projects Paraguay 2026 GDP Growth at 4.4%, Praises Inflation Targeting Framework (2026-06-29)
events.summary: The IMF completed its Article IV consultation mission to Paraguay (June 15-26). Key projections: 2026 GDP growth of 4.4%, converging to 3.8% medium-term. The IMF praised Paraguay's inflation targeting regime, flexible exchange rate, and fiscal discipline. Paraguay was largely insulated from the Middle East conflict due to 100% renewable electricity generation and favorable soybean production/prices. The IMF sees scope for gradual further rate easing if energy shocks prove temporary.

events.title: President Peña Delivers Third Annual Report: 2025 GDP Growth at 6.6% (12-Year High), Unemployment Falls to 5.3% Historic Q1 Low (2026-07-01)
events.summary: President Santiago Peña presented his third annual management report to Congress. Key metrics: 2025 GDP growth of 6.6% (highest in 12 years, #1 in Latin America); Q1 2026 growth of 5.8%; Q4 2025 unemployment at 3.6% (historic low); poverty at 16% and extreme poverty at 2.4% (both historic lows); IPS formal employment at a record 842,023; two investment-grade ratings obtained (Moody's and S&P).

events.title: BCP Holds Policy Rate at 5.50% for Fourth Consecutive Month; June CPI at Just 2.09% YoY (2026-07-02)
events.summary: The BCP unanimously held the benchmark rate at 5.50% in June, maintaining a neutral stance since February 2026. Latest CPI data (AE_IPC-26.6) shows June CPI fell 0.28% MoM with annual inflation at just 2.09%, well below the 3.5% target. Next policy meeting is July 23; markets expect rates to remain unchanged through year-end. The BCP flagged Middle East conflict and US tariff uncertainty as key external risks.

events.title: Guarani Appreciates 21.9% YoY: USD/PYG Falls from 7,784 to 6,082, Hitting Customs Revenue and Border Trade (2026-07-03)
events.summary: The Guarani appreciated 21.9% year-on-year against the USD, from PYG 7,784 to PYG 6,081.67. Customs revenue fell 11.6% in H1 2026 despite import volumes rising 7% and import values rising 10% - the strong currency 'liquefied' the Guarani tax base. Total DNIT revenue reached PYG 21.73 trillion, up only 1.8% YoY. Border trade was severely affected: daily Argentine shoppers at Alberdi-Formosa plummeted from 1,200 to 400-500.

sections.title: II. Political & Policy Developments
sections.description: Major legislation, policy adjustments, foreign investment regulation, tax reform, investment incentives

events.title: Pena Administration Passes 164 Laws: Historic Reforms in Tax Incentives, Railway Liberalization, Pension Reform (2026-07-01)
events.summary: President Pena highlighted political stability as the foundation for reform in his annual report. The administration passed 164 laws, including: a new Investment Incentives Law (replacing Law 60/90), Capital Markets Law (approaching OECD standards), Data Protection Law, pension system reform, and Railway Sector Liberalization Law (7665/2026). The new investment incentives framework modernizes tax benefits for both domestic and foreign investors.

events.title: Paraguay and Chile Sign Double Taxation Agreement, Expanding International Tax Treaty Network (2026-07 Early)
events.summary: Paraguay and Chile signed a Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement, further expanding Paraguay's international tax treaty network following agreements with Uruguay and UAE. The agreement reduces withholding tax rates on cross-border dividends, interest, and royalties (as low as 5-10%), enhancing Paraguay's competitiveness as a regional investment hub.

events.title: Paraguay Opens Railway Sector to International Capital: Etihad Rail Invests USD 480M in Asuncion Commuter Rail (Effective 2026-06-10)
events.summary: Law 7665/2026 expands the Commuter Rail Law and introduces a Government-to-Government (G2G) agreement regime. Etihad Rail PJSC (UAE) will construct Phase I (Asuncion-Luque, 18km, USD 480M) through a Paraguayan SPV (75% UAE / 25% Paraguay). Key features: irrevocable USD deferred payment obligations, AFD trust guarantee, international arbitration, and comprehensive tax/customs exemptions - a major innovation in Paraguay's infrastructure financing model.

sections.title: III. Social & Security Situation
sections.description: Labor market, social stability, public security, employment data

events.title: Record Employment: Q1 Unemployment at Historic Low of 5.3%, Formal Employment Exceeds 842,000; 7 of 10 New Non-Agricultural Jobs Are Formal (2026-07-01)
events.summary: President Pena's report disclosed: Q4 2025 unemployment at 3.6% (historic low), Q1 2026 at 5.3% (lowest Q1 on record). IPS formal employment exceeded 842,023 - a new record - with 134,000 new contributors since August 2023. The formalization rate surpassed 40% for the first time. Seven out of ten new non-agricultural jobs created in the past year were formal, signaling significant progress in labor formalization.

events.title: Security Situation Improves Significantly: Vehicle Robbery Down 39%, Motorcycle Robbery Down 38%; 10,000 New Police, Boton Lince Rapid Response System Launched (2026-07-02)
events.summary: Security metrics from the presidential report: 10,000 new police officers added in two years (5,000 each in 2025 and 2026); aggravated vehicle robbery down 39%; motorcycle robbery down 38%. 'Boton Lince' mobile app rolled out, achieving sub-4-minute police response in critical zones. SENAD executed 8,947 anti-drug operations, inflicting USD 212 million in losses on narcotrafficking. Pena declared: 'Paraguay has ceased to be known as Latin America's cocaine corridor.'

events.title: Chilean President Kast Visits Paraguay, Calls for Regional Unity Against Organized Crime; Paraguay Joins 'Santiago Commitment' (2026-07-01)
events.summary: Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast made his first official visit to Paraguay, meeting with President Pena. Kast called for regional unity against organized crime, stating 'neutrality is not an option in the face of organized crime.' Paraguay joined the 'Santiago Commitment' promoted by Chile, alongside Argentina, Bolivia, Ecuador, and Peru, strengthening information sharing and joint law enforcement against transnational crime.

sections.title: IV. International Relations & Diplomacy
sections.description: Paraguay's relations with major powers, Mercosur dynamics, cross-strait relations, multilateral engagement

events.title: Mercosur Summit Controversy: Paraguay Demands 25% EU Export Quota Share; Pena Calls Current System 'Unfair, Unacceptable' (2026-07-01)
events.summary: At the Mercosur Summit in Asuncion, Paraguay lodged a strong protest against EU trade agreement quota distribution. President Pena called the current 'first-come, first-served' system 'unfair, offensive, and unacceptable' for Paraguay. Paraguay demands a fixed 25% allocation by product category, while Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay favor allocation based on historical export averages. Paraguay linked the quota debate to strengthening FOCEM structural convergence funds, demanding greater compensation for landlocked countries' logistics costs. The EU-Mercosur FTA provisionally entered force on May 1; Uruguay assumes the rotating presidency from July.

events.title: Paraguay's China/Taiwan Policy: FM Reaffirms Willingness to Trade with China but 'Won't Abandon Taiwan'; China Says 'Unacceptable' (2026-07-01)
events.summary: During the Mercosur Summit, FM Ramirez Lezcano reiterated that Paraguay is willing to negotiate trade with China within the Mercosur framework, but will not condition this on abandoning relations with Taiwan. China's Foreign Ministry responded that Paraguay is 'on the wrong side of history' and cannot 'maintain Taiwan ties while trading with China.' Brazil's President Lula is pushing Mercosur to initiate trade talks with China, adding pressure on Paraguay - the only bloc member without diplomatic relations with Beijing.

events.title: Paraguay Elected Vice President of 81st UN General Assembly; Preparing 70th Anniversary of Taiwan Diplomatic Relations in 2027 (2026-06-29)
events.summary: Paraguay was elected Vice President of the 81st UN General Assembly session (2026-2027). Taiwan congratulated Paraguay and expressed appreciation for its continued support for Taiwan's participation in international organizations. In mid-June, Taiwan's Deputy FM Chen Ming-chi visited Asuncion, reviewing progress since Pena's May visit to Taiwan and advancing US-Taiwan-Paraguay trilateral cooperation in AI, 5G, and cybersecurity. Both sides are preparing a commemorative agenda for the 70th anniversary of diplomatic relations in 2027.

events.title: Paraguay Deepens US Cooperation: Advancing Beef Market Access, Comprehensive Defense Cooperation Upgrade (2026-06 to 07)
events.summary: Paraguay continues to deepen strategic cooperation with the US. In June, Pena met with Secretary of State Rubio to discuss beef quotas, direct flight routes, nuclear energy cooperation, and digital infrastructure. In May, the FM met with USTR Deputy Representative in Washington to advance Paraguayan beef market access under the TIFA framework. On defense: SOFA agreement signed, Massachusetts National Guard SPP partnership marks 25 years, and Northrop Grumman radar system negotiations are accelerating.

sections.title: V. Industry Focus: Telecom, Digital Energy & AI
sections.description: 5G spectrum & commercial deployment, fiber infrastructure, digital energy investment, AI data center development, industry regulation

events.title: CONATEL Completes Public Consultation on 2.3GHz/3.5GHz Spectrum Tender; Final Bidding Documents Expected H2 2026 (2026-07)
events.summary: CONATEL Resolution 790/2026 launched public consultation on tender terms for 2,300MHz and 3,500MHz bands for mobile broadband and 5G services; submissions closed May 15. Resolution 3339/2025 had already redesignated 3,700-3,800MHz for IMT (5G NR), configuring 3.3-3.8GHz as 10x50MHz TDD sub-bands. Final bidding documents expected H2 2026, specifying coverage obligations, QoS standards, and investment commitments.

events.title: HIVE Digital Launches BUZZ Cloud AI Platform in Paraguay: Tier III Data Center, 300MW Hydro Capacity, 100MW Expansion Planned (2026-06)
events.summary: HIVE Digital Technologies (NASDAQ: HIVE) officially launched its BUZZ Cloud AI platform in Asuncion, hosted in a Tier III data center in partnership with Paraguay's leading telecom operator. The platform leverages Paraguay's national dark fiber network and 300MW of surplus hydroelectric capacity (Itaipu/Yacyreta), with a further 100MW expansion planned in 2026. GPU clusters will serve AI training, inference, and data-intensive workloads for South American clients. HIVE total Paraguay capacity now at 400MW (540MW globally).

events.title: Paraguay-Taiwan AI Data Center JV: Phase 1 at 10MW, Phase 3 Targeting ~1GW as 'World's Largest AI Center' (Announced May 2026, Ongoing)
events.summary: President Pena highlighted Taiwan AI cooperation in his annual report: a 50/50 JV for AI data center construction - Phase 1 at 10MW, Phase 2 scaling to 100MW, and Phase 3 targeting approximately 1GW, potentially the world's largest AI data center. Paraguay leverages 100% renewable hydropower, Decreto 5306/2026 (special USD-denominated AI/cloud tariffs with 15-year contracts), and Decreto 5307/2026 (Power-to-X). The IDB is providing USD 130 million to support digital infrastructure modernization.

events.title: MITIC Digital Transformation Report: 18,000km Fiber, 1,600 Starlink Terminals, 3,234 Schools Connected (2026-07)
events.summary: President Pena's report highlighted MITIC's role in digital transformation. As of June 2026: national fiber optic network reaches 18,000km, including 1,000+ km newly activated in Neembucu department; 1,600 Starlink satellite terminals deployed with SpaceX for remote schools and health centers; 400+ free public WiFi points nationwide serving 1.3M+ citizens; 3,234 educational institutions connected to internet, benefiting 1M+ students; Villa Hayes National Tier III Data Center and Innova Technology Park under construction.

sections.title: VI. Key Client Movements
sections.description: Tracking strategic moves, investment plans, network deployment, and technology choices of major Paraguayan telecom clients

events.title: Claro - 5G Commercial Launch Imminent; USD 35M Initial Deployment; Mobile Core 5G-Upgraded (2026-07)
events.summary: Claro (America Movil) won 200MHz in the 3.5-3.7GHz band (license fee ~USD 2M) in the August 2025 auction, deploying an initial USD 35M for 5G across 12 key metropolitan areas. Under the 6-month deployment obligation, commercial services expected in Q2 2026, starting in Greater Asuncion. Mobile core network upgraded for 5G. Requirements: 100 base stations per 100MHz, 10% serving government entities. Claro poised to become Paraguay's first major commercial 5G operator.

events.title: Tigo - Did Not Participate in 5G Auction; Focused on 4G/Fiber Expansion; Secured USD 100M BID Invest+Proparco Financing (2026-07)
events.summary: Tigo (Millicom), Paraguay's largest mobile operator (3.2M users, 47.3% share), withdrew from the August 2025 5G auction due to Chinese vendor (Huawei/ZTE) restrictions. Current focus: 3G-to-4G migration, FTTH expansion, Tigo Money fintech growth. In March 2026, BID Invest and Proparco invested USD 100M in Millicom bonds covering network modernization in 7 countries including Paraguay. In January 2026, Tigo Paraguay completed a historic USD 77M Guarani bond issuance. The company continues alternative 5G spectrum negotiations with the government.

events.title: Personal - Did Not Bid in 5G Auction; Maintains Low-Cost Positioning; Risks Losing Third-Operator Status to Nubicom (2026-07)
events.summary: Personal (Telecom Argentina), with ~2.4M users (35.5% share), also did not participate in the 5G auction due to Chinese vendor restrictions and has announced no independent 5G deployment plans. The company continues to focus on the low-cost segment, with coverage concentrated in urban areas and weak outside Asuncion. Without network upgrades, Personal risks losing third-operator status to Nubicom. No significant infrastructure investment announcements.

events.title: Nubicom - New Entrant, USD 200M 5G Build-from-Scratch Investment; Commercial Launch Expected Q2 2026 (2026-07)
events.summary: Nubicom (fixed internet provider from Salta, Argentina) won 200MHz in the 3.3-3.5GHz band (license fee ~USD 2M) and announced a USD 200M investment - Paraguay's largest single 5G deployment. Must establish local subsidiary within 6 weeks and build mobile infrastructure from scratch, with at least 100 base stations per 100MHz. As an operator with no prior mobile infrastructure, building a new network presents challenges but also creates a major market opportunity for equipment vendors and infrastructure partners.

sections.title: VII. Comprehensive Enterprise Impact Analysis
sections.description: Integrating macro trends, industry dynamics, and client movements to assess Paraguay's enterprise operating environment
sections.impact_analysis:
## I. Cost Dimension 

Comprehensive assessment of cost pressures based on this week's data:

- **Exchange Rate Costs**: The Guarani appreciated 21.9% YoY (USD/PYG from 7,784 to 6,082), among the strongest currencies in the region. USD-denominated operating costs (local salaries, service procurement) rise significantly, squeezing export margins. However, imported equipment and raw material costs are significantly lower, benefiting import-dependent sectors such as telecom and data centers.
- **Labor Costs**: The 5% minimum wage increase (effective July 1) is moderate and aligns with inflation (June CPI just 2.09% YoY). Real unit labor costs remain manageable. Formal employment rate exceeding 40% and IPS contributors at 842,023 signal a tightening but still affordable labor market.
- **Energy Costs**: Decreto 5306/2026 and 5307/2026 offer USD-denominated special tariffs with up to 15-year fixed terms, creating among the world's most competitive energy cost structures for data centers and AI enterprises. HIVE Digital and X8 Cloud validate this advantage. However, the Villeta tariff policy reversal reminds that energy costs depend on policy continuity.
- **Tax Costs**: The strong Guarani caused customs revenue to fall 11.6% in H1 2026 (despite import volumes +7%). DNIT total revenue grew only 1.8%, far below the 13.4% annual target. This may trigger new tax enforcement measures or policy adjustments in H2 2026.

## II. Market Dimension 

Paraguay's market opportunities are expanding significantly in digital infrastructure and investment facilitation:

- **5G & Telecom Equipment Market**: CONATEL's new 2.3/3.5GHz spectrum tender expected in H2 2026, creating procurement opportunities for equipment and infrastructure vendors. Claro and Nubicom's deployment obligations (100 base stations each per 100MHz) mean at least 200 5G base stations' worth of demand in the near term. US-backed equipment exclusion policies favor non-Chinese suppliers.
- **AI & Data Center Supply Chain**: HIVE BUZZ Cloud launch, Paraguay-Taiwan AI data center JV (Phase 1: 10MW to Phase 3: ~1GW), and X8 Cloud (up to USD 50B) will drive demand for: power equipment, cooling systems, fiber connectivity, cybersecurity, professional IT services. IDB's USD 130M digital facility provides additional funding.
- **Infrastructure & Logistics**: Railway Law 7665/2026 brings Etihad Rail's USD 480M commuter rail project, creating opportunities in rail equipment, engineering, and operations. G2G model's irrevocable USD payments provide supplier payment security.
- **EU Market Access**: EU-Mercosur FTA provisionally effective since May 1, but quota allocation unresolved. If Paraguay secures 25% quota, beef, poultry, sugar exports surge. If 'first-come, first-served' persists, Argentina and Brazil will continue capturing most quotas.

## III. Compliance Dimension 

The compliance environment is generally improving but requires monitoring of policy volatility:

- **Investment Facilitation**: Investor Pass (Decreto 0283/2026) and updated immigration requirements in effect with four investment pathways (min USD 70K/5 jobs to permanent residency). Dividend tax cut from 15% to 8% provides substantial benefits.
- **Tax Treaties**: Chile DTA signing marks further internationalization of Paraguay's tax compliance framework. Lower withholding rates improve investment returns.
- **Labor Compliance**: WhatsApp minimum wage complaint hotline signals increased enforcement. Companies should complete payroll compliance audits following July 1 wage adjustment.
- **Fiscal Risk**: IMF Article IV noted 2026 deficit may overshoot targets due to supplier arrears (USD 220M construction + ~USD 500M pharmaceuticals). Monitor potential tax adjustments to close the gap.

## Overall Assessment

The 24 monitored events this week (8 from government sources) paint a picture of sustained macroeconomic strength (IMF projects 2026 GDP growth 4.4%, inflation just 2.09%). However, enterprises must maintain risk sensitivity amid strong Guarani impacts, heated EU-Mercosur quota disputes, and occasional energy policy reversals. The wave of investment in digital infrastructure and AI represents this cycle's most prominent structural opportunity.

sections.title: VIII. China-Specific Enterprise Risk & Opportunity Analysis
sections.description: Tailored analysis for Chinese enterprises operating in or considering entry into Paraguay, covering diplomatic risks, policy risks, and strategic recommendations
sections.impact_analysis:
## I. Risk Warnings

High Priority:

- **Diplomatic Barriers Continually Strengthening**: At the Mercosur Summit, Paraguay's FM publicly reiterated 'willing to trade with China but won't abandon Taiwan.' China explicitly stated this is 'unacceptable.' Brazil (Lula) pushing Mercosur toward China talks adds pressure, but no near-term policy shift expected. Chinese enterprises face informal barriers in project approvals and heightened political scrutiny.
- **Telecom Equipment Supplier Exclusion Institutionalized**: CONATEL substantively excluded Huawei/ZTE through 5G auction rules ('trade reciprocity' clause), now formally executed via Claro and Nubicom spectrum awards. New 2.3/3.5GHz tender expected to maintain identical rules. Exclusion may extend to other critical infrastructure sectors (data centers, smart city projects) through 'cybersecurity' and 'supply chain security' narratives.

Medium Priority:

- **US-Taiwan-Paraguay Triangle Deepening**: Paraguay's accession to the 'Santiago Commitment,' SOFA agreement, Northrop Grumman radar procurement, and US-Taiwan-Paraguay trilateral AI/5G/cybersecurity cooperation further entrench the architecture excluding Chinese enterprises. In sensitive infrastructure projects, Chinese firms face systemic access barriers, not just commercial competition.
- **Exchange Rate Risk**: Guarani's 21.9% YoY appreciation makes it Latin America's strongest currency. RMB-equivalent profits for Chinese enterprises already in Paraguay have significantly shrunk. Hedging strategies require evaluation.
- **Fiscal Adjustment Risk**: DNIT H1 2026 revenue grew only 1.8%, far below 13.4% annual target. H2 2026 may see new tax enforcement measures (strengthened transfer pricing reviews, import valuation adjustments), affecting Chinese enterprises' tax compliance costs.

## II. Opportunity Analysis

Actionable Opportunities:

- **Non-Equipment Roles in Digital Infrastructure**: Despite telecom equipment access restrictions, HIVE, Paraguay-Taiwan AI data center, and X8 Cloud projects demonstrate strong demand for data center construction, renewable energy integration, cooling systems, fiber cabling, power equipment, and EPC services. Chinese enterprises can explore complementary roles: electrical equipment (transformers, UPS, power distribution), cooling solutions, solar-plus-storage, data center construction engineering.
- **Agri-Tech & Green Transformation**: Paraguay's economy is anchored by soybean and beef exports (GDP growth 6.6% largely agriculture-driven). Strong demand for precision agriculture, IoT sensors, supply chain digitization, and cold chain logistics. Chinese agri-tech enterprises can compete in areas not triggering security reviews.
- **Mercosur Indirect Channel**: Chinese enterprises already in Brazil or Argentina can leverage the EU-Mercosur FTA for preferential EU export access. Paraguay's quota dispute provides a window to observe and influence Mercosur trade governance.
- **New Energy & Power-to-X**: Decreto 5307/2026 offers USD-denominated tariffs and long-term contracts for green hydrogen, ammonia, methanol, and synthetic fuels. Paraguay's surplus hydroelectric resources provide globally competitive energy costs. China's electrolyzer and green methanol technology finds potential application here.

## III. Strategic Recommendations

**Immediate Actions:**
- Update labor compliance and residency documentation against July 1 new minimum wage and Immigration Resolution 407/2026 requirements.
- Assess financial impact of 21.9% Guarani appreciation on existing Paraguay operations in USD/RMB terms. Evaluate FX hedging needs.

**Short-Term (1-3 Months):**
- Closely monitor CONATEL's new 2.3/3.5GHz spectrum tender progress. Explore pathways for participation through third-country subsidiaries (e.g., European entities) for complementary equipment and services.
- Proactively engage HIVE Digital, X8 Cloud, and Paraguay-Taiwan AI data center projects for infrastructure ancillary demands (power, cooling, construction) as non-sensitive suppliers.
- Arrange on-the-ground policy research in Asuncion, establishing direct channels with MIC, ANDE, and MITIC for timely policy updates.

**Medium-Term (3-12 Months):**
- Study indirect market access strategies through other Mercosur countries (Brazil/Argentina), leveraging EU-Mercosur FTA for 'curved entry' into Paraguay.
- Evaluate investment feasibility in green hydrogen and Power-to-X, capitalizing on Decreto 5307/2026 policy window and Paraguay's energy cost advantages.
- Continuously monitor Paraguay's foreign policy trajectory - any future adjustment in China relations would open new market access dynamics. Recommend quarterly Paraguay macro-political risk assessment updates.
